subject: Hosting classification for penetration-test evidence — which systems are covered
messages:
From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@stellardata.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pen test evidence — which hosting types are in-scope?

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well. We’re compiling the security evidence package for Stellar Data’s SIG and need a clear statement on which hosting variants Redwood includes in its penetration-test reports. Our auditor has specifically asked: 1) Does the standard Redwood pen-test report include Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools) that you run for customers? 2) For Private/VPC deployments, do you include customer-managed compute or only the Redwood-managed control plane? 3) For on-prem installations, do you provide any test artifacts or is that entirely customer-delivered?

We want to map Redwood’s artifacts to SIG questions and make sure we don’t ask for items you won’t provide. If you have a short matrix or a sample report stub you can share, that would be ideal.

Thanks — can we aim to close this today?

Tom Blake
Security Operations Manager
Stellar Data Inc.

---
Attachments: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@stellardata.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence — which hosting types are in-scope?

Tom — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Karthik (security) and Laura (compliance) to provide the canonical mapping. Below is a quick, high-level proposal from my side so we have something actionable for your auditor:

Proposed in-scope summary (high level):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood-managed control plane + runtime hosts are in-scope. We can provide the pen-test summary and host/network findings.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Redwood-managed GPU pools are covered for infrastructure we control (hosts, network). Tenancy/isolation tests are included where Redwood manages the underlying compute; customer data plane connectors that run in customer-managed VPCs are out-of-scope.
- Private / VPC-delivered Private: If the customer uses Redwood Private with Redwood-managed tenancy inside our VPCs, we include the same artifacts as hosted. For customer-hosted VPCs (customer-managed compute) we only provide the control-plane artifacts and guidance; customer-owned compute is not tested unless part of an agreed engagement.
- On-prem: On-prem deployments are typically out-of-scope for our pen test unless we are engaged for a custom assessment — we can provide a checklist of evidence customers should run locally.

If that aligns with you, Karthik can confirm the exact artifact names and any recent report stubs. If you prefer, we can jump on a quick 20-minute call to walk the auditor through the mapping.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Attachments: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@stellardata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test evidence — which hosting types are in-scope? (detailed mapping & artifacts)

Hi Tom — thanks for the note and Marissa for the tidy summary. Below is the canonical mapping we provide to auditors and customers; I’m attaching our latest pen-test summary and an asset inventory extract to illustrate.

Canonical scope mapping (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API / managed): FULL in-scope for Redwood-managed compute, networking, auth services, and runtime instances. We provide: penetration-test executive summary, technical findings (host/network), remediation status, and screenshots/log excerpts where appropriate. (Attachment: 20260515-redwood-pen-test-summary.pdf)

- Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated / reserved capacity): IN-SCOPE for Redwood-controlled infrastructure (physical/VM hosts in our pools, hypervisor/network configuration, orchestration services). Tenant separation/authorization logic is included. Out-of-scope: customer-managed VPC endpoints and any customer-hosted connector appliances. We provide an indicator in the report which components are tenant-specific and which are multi-tenant.

- Private / VPC options: TWO CASES —
  * Redwood-managed Private: if Redwood operates the Private environment (we provision and manage the compute within our cloud accounts) the environment is in-scope and we provide standard artifacts.
  * Customer-managed Private/VPC: if the customer deploys Redwood components into their VPC or on their cloud accounts (customer owned compute or direct VPC peering where compute runs in customer project), then penetration testing of that customer-owned compute is the customer’s responsibility. We still provide control-plane artifacts, configuration baselines, and guidance.

- On-prem: OUT-OF-SCOPE for standard Redwood pen tests. For customers who need on-prem assessments we coordinate a separate statement of work; otherwise we provide a local checklist and recommended OS/hardening baseline.

Remediation status (recent):
- Critical findings from 2026 pen test: 0 open
- High: 1 open (mitigation planned; ETA 2026-08-10)
- Medium/Low: tracked in our backlog; remediation windows and compensating controls documented in the attached inventory extract.

Attachments included: 20260515-redwood-pen-test-summary.pdf (executive + technical findings), asset-inventory-20260630.csv (mapping of services to hosting classification).

If you send the auditor contact, we can provide a short cover letter mapping Redwood artifacts to SIG control IDs (e.g., SIG A.2.1 -> pen-test-exec-summary.pdf).

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Security Engineering
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (510) 555-0148

Karthik — this is perfect, thanks. The distinction on "Redwood-managed Private" vs "Customer-managed Private" is exactly what the auditor needed. We have the pen-test stub and inventory listed; can you also confirm you’ll provide the cover letter mapping to SIG control IDs and a single-page statement we can include in our SIG that calls out the one open High finding and its mitigation ETA? If so that will close out our request.

Appreciate the quick turnaround today.

Tom
